62:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Jumu'ah It is a city On the authority of Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with them, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite Surat Al-Jumu’ah and Surat Al-Munafiqun in the Friday prayer. Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God Almighty tells us that everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, that is, all creatures, both speaking and inanimate, as God Almighty said: There is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise. Then God Almighty said: The Sovereign, the Holy, that is, He is the Owner of the heavens and the earth, who disposes of them with His wisdom. He is the Sanctified, that is, He is free from imperfections and described with attributes of perfection. The Exalted in Might, the Wise, the explanation of which has been presented more than once. God the Almighty said: It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from themselves (Al-Isra’ 1:11) The unlettered are the Arabs, as God the Almighty said: “And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered, ‘Have you submitted?’ If they have submitted, then they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, upon you is only the conveyance. And God is Seeing of the servants.” (Al-Isra’ 1:12) The specific mention of the unlettered does not negate all others, but the favor upon them is more eloquent and greater, as God the Almighty said in His saying: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, which is a reminder for others by which they are reminded. Likewise, God the Almighty said: And warn your nearest relatives. This and similar verses do not contradict His saying: Say, ‘O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all,’ and His saying: To warn you and whomever it reaches. And His saying, in describing the Qur’an: And whoever disbelieves in it from the parties - the Fire is his promised destination. (Al-Isra’ 1:12) and other verses indicating the universality of his mission, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, to all of creation, red and black alike. We have already explained this in Surat Al-An’am with verses and authentic hadiths, and all praise and thanks are due to God. This verse is the confirmation of God’s answer to His friend Abraham, when he prayed to the people of Mecca that God send among them a Messenger from among themselves, who would recite to them His verses, purify them, and teach them the Book and wisdom. So God Almighty sent him, praise and thanks be to Him, at a time when the messengers had ceased and the paths had been obliterated, and the need for him was great, and God hated the people of the earth, Arabs and non-Arabs, except for the remnants of the People of the Book, that is, a small number of those who held fast to what God sent Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. For this reason, God Almighty said: “It is He who has sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves, reciting to them His verses and purifying them and teaching them the Book and wisdom - although they were before in manifest error.” This is because the Arabs had long held fast to the religion of Abraham, the friend of God, peace be upon him, but they changed it, altered it, reversed it, and opposed it, replacing monotheism with polytheism and certainty with doubt, and they innovated things that God had not permitted. Likewise, the People of the Book changed their books, distorted them, altered them, and interpreted them. Then God sent Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. With a great, complete law that is comprehensive for all creation, in which is their guidance and clarification of all that they need for their life and their afterlife, and calling them to that which brings them closer to Paradise and the pleasure of God with them, and forbidding that which brings them closer to the Fire and the wrath of God the Most High, a judge and decider of all doubts, suspicions and skepticism in the fundamentals and branches, and for Him the Most High, praise and thanks be to Him, gathered all the good qualities of those who came before him and gave him what He did not give to anyone of the first and will not give to anyone of the last, so may the prayers and peace of God be upon him forever until the Day of Judgment. And the Almighty said: “And others among them have not yet joined them. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” Imam Abu Abdullah al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, said: Abdul Aziz bin Abdullah told us, Sulayman bin Bilal told us, on the authority of Thawr, on the authority of Abu al-Ghaith, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when Surat al-Jumu’ah was revealed to him: And others among them have not yet joined them. They said: Who are they, O Messenger of God? He did not return to them until he was asked three times, and among us was Salman al-Farsi. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed his hand on Salman al-Farsi and then said: If faith were at the Pleiades, men - or a man - from these would attain it. Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Jarir narrated it through various chains of transmission, on the authority of Thawr ibn Zayd al-Dailami, on the authority of Salim Abu al-Ghaith, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with this chain of transmission. In this hadith is evidence that this surah was revealed in Medina and that his mission, may God bless him and grant him peace, was universal to all people, because he interpreted the words of God, the Most High, and others among them, as meaning the Persians. For this reason, he wrote his letters to the Persians, the Romans, and other nations, calling them to God, the Almighty, and to follow what he brought. For this reason, Mujahid and more than one other said about the words of God, the Most High, and others among them who have not yet joined them, that they are the non-Arabs and everyone who believed in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the non-Arabs. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibrahim ibn al-Ala’ al-Zubaidi told us, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, Abu Muhammad ‘Isa ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d al-Sa’idi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God the Almighty said: Indeed, in the loins of the loins are men and women of my nation who will enter Paradise without account. Then he recited: And others of them who have not yet joined them. Meaning the rest of the nation of Muhammad the Almighty. And His statement: And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Meaning: Possessor of might and wisdom in His law and decree. And His statement: That is the bounty of God which He bestows upon whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty. Meaning what God the Almighty gave to Muhammad the great prophethood and what He specifically gave to his nation by sending him the Almighty to them.

62:5: God Almighty says, blaming the Jews who were given the Torah and carried it to act upon it, but then did not act upon it: Their example in this is like that of a donkey carrying books, that is, like a donkey carrying books, not knowing what is in them, so it carries them physically and does not know what is upon it. Likewise, these people in carrying the book that they were given, they memorized it verbally and did not understand it nor act upon its requirements, rather they interpreted it, distorted it and changed it, so they are in a worse state than donkeys, because donkeys do not understand, while these people do understand and do not use it. For this reason God Almighty said in another verse: “Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. It is those who are the heedless.” And God Almighty said here: “Evil is the example of the people who deny the signs of God. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.” Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever speaks on Friday while the imam is delivering the sermon is like a donkey carrying books, and the one who tells him to be quiet has no Friday prayer. Then God Almighty said: Say, ‘O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of God to the exclusion of mankind, then wish for death, if you should be truthful.’ That is, if you claim that you are on the right path and that Muhammad and his companions are astray, then call for death for the one who has gone astray from the two groups if you are truthful, that is, in what you claim. God the Almighty said: And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forth meaning what they have done of disbelief, injustice and immorality. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers. We have already discussed this Mubahala with the Jews in Surat Al-Baqarah, where God the Almighty said: “Say: If the home of the Hereafter with God is exclusively for you, to the exclusion of all other people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful. And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forth. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers. And you will find them the most greedy of people for life, and even more so than those who associate others with God. One of them would like to live a thousand years, but that long life will not remove him from the punishment. And God is Seeing of what they do.” We have already discussed there, and explained that what is meant is that they should call upon themselves or their opponents to go astray, as the Mubahala with the Christians was mentioned in Al Imran 3:“So whoever disputes with you concerning him after what has come to you of knowledge, say: Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then supplicate earnestly and invoke the curse of God upon the liars.” And the Mubahala with the polytheists in Surat Maryam 19:“Say: Whoever is in error, let the Most Merciful extend to him a term. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail bin Yazid al-Raqi, Abu Zaid, told us, Furat told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim bin Malik al-Jazari, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Abu Jahl, may God curse him, said: If I see Muhammad at the Kaaba, I will come to him and step on his neck. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If he did, the angels would seize him right there. If the Jews wished for death, they would die and see their places in Hell. If those who engaged in Mubahalah with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were to go out, they would return without finding family or wealth.” Narrated by al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abd al-Karim. Al-Bukhari said: Amr bin Khalid followed him, on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Amr, on the authority of Abd al-Karim. Al-Nasa’i also narrated it on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Ubaydullah al-Halabi, on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Amr al-Raqi, with a more complete chain of transmission. And the Almighty said: “Say: ‘Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.’” Like His Almighty’s saying in Surat An-Nisa’: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you were within fortified towers. And in the Mu’jam of At-Tabarani from the hadith of Mu’adh ibn Muhammad Al-Hudhali from Yunus from Al-Hasan from Samurah with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The example of one who flees from death is like that of a fox whom the earth pursues for a debt. So he comes running until, when he is exhausted and dazed, he enters his hole. 62:9: Friday is called Jumu'ah because it is derived from the word 'gathering' to gather. The Muslims gather on it once a week in the great temples. On this day, all creation was perfected, for it is the sixth day of the six days on which God created the heavens and the earth. On this day, He created Adam, on this day He admitted him to Paradise, on this day he was expelled from it, on this day the Hour will come, and on this day there is an hour when no believing servant asks God for something good except that He will give it to him, as proven in the authentic hadiths. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah told us, 'Ubaydah ibn Humayd told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Ma'shar, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of 'Alqamah, on the authority of Qurta' al-Dhabi, who told us: Salman said: Abu al-Qasim, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Salman, what is Friday? I said: God and His Messenger know best. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Friday is the day on which God gathered your parents - or your father. Similar words were narrated from Abu Hurayrah, and God knows best. It was called in the ancient language the Day of Arabism, and it has been proven that the nations before us were ordered to do it but they deviated from it. The Jews chose Saturday, on which Adam was not created, and the Christians chose Sunday, on which creation began. God chose for this nation Friday, on which God completed creation, as Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from the hadith of Abd Al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurairah narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “We are the last and the first on the Day of Resurrection. However, they were given the Book before us. Then this is their day that God imposed upon them, and they differed about it, so God guided us to it. So the people follow us on it. The Jews will be tomorrow and the Christians the day after tomorrow.” This is the wording of Al-Bukhari. In a wording of Muslim: “God led those before us astray from Friday, so the Jews had Saturday, and the Christians had Sunday, so God brought us and guided us to Friday, so He made Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. And likewise they will follow us on the Day of Resurrection. We are the last of the people of this world, and the first on the Day of Resurrection, and the judgment will be between them before all creation.” God has commanded the believers to gather to worship Him on Friday, as He says: O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Jumu’ah, then proceed to the remembrance of God. That is, go straight ahead, be intentional, and be attentive in your walk to it. What is meant by striding here is not walking quickly, but rather being attentive to it, as God says: And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the necessary effort while he is a believer. Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with them used to recite it: Then hasten to the remembrance of God. As for walking quickly to prayer, it has been forbidden, as they reported in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “When you hear the call to prayer, then walk to the prayer with tranquility and dignity, and do not rush. Pray whatever you catch up with, and complete whatever you miss.” This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Abu Qatadah said: While we were praying with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he heard the noise of men. When he had finished, he said: What is the matter with you? They said: We rushed to the prayer. He said: "Do not do that. When you come to the prayer, walk and be tranquil. Pray whatever you catch up with, and complete whatever you miss." `Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: "When the prayer is called, do not come running, but come walking, with tranquility and dignity. Pray whatever you catch up with, and complete whatever you miss." At-Tirmidhi narrated it in this way from the hadith of `Abd al-Razzaq. He narrated it via Yazid ibn Zari` from Muammar from al-Zuhri from Abu Salamah from Abu Hurayrah, similarly. Al-Hasan said: By God, it is not about walking on foot, and they were forbidden to come to the prayer except with tranquility and dignity, but with the heart, intention, and humility. Qatada said about His statement: So strive to the remembrance of God meaning that you strive with your heart and your actions, which is walking to it. He interpreted the statement of God Almighty: And when he reached the age of striving with him as meaning walking with him. Something similar was narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Zayd ibn Aslam, and others. It is recommended for the one who comes to the Friday prayer to take a bath before coming to it, as it was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When one of you comes to the Friday prayer, let him take a bath. And they both have on the authority of Abu Sa’id, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Taking a bath on Friday is obligatory for every adult. And on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God’s right over every Muslim is that he take a bath every seven days, washing his head and his body. Narrated by Muslim. And on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is obligatory for every Muslim man every seven days to take a bath on one day, which is Friday. Narrated by Ahmad, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Hibban. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Adam told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Awza’i, on the authority of Hassan ibn Atiyah, on the authority of Abu al-Ash’ath al-San’ani, on the authority of Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafi, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever performs ghusl and bathes on Friday, and comes early and walks and does not ride, and draws close to the imam and listens and does not engage in idle talk, will have for every step the reward of a year of fasting and praying.” This hadith has various chains of transmission and wordings, and it was narrated by the four scholars of Sunan, and al-Tirmidhi classed it as hasan. Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever performs ghusl on Friday, the ghusl for major ritual impurity, then goes in the first hour, it is as if he sacrificed a camel. Whoever goes in the second hour, it is as if he sacrificed a cow. Whoever goes in the third hour, it is as if he sacrificed a horned ram. Whoever goes in the fourth hour, it is as if he sacrificed a chicken. Whoever goes in the fifth hour, it is as if he sacrificed an egg. When the imam comes out, the angels are present and listen to the remembrance.” Narrated by both of them. It is recommended that he wear his best clothes, clean himself, use a miswak, clean himself and purify himself. And in the hadith of Abu Saeed mentioned above, Ghusl on Friday is obligatory for every adult, as is the siwak, and to touch some of his family’s perfume. Imam Ahmad said: Ya’qub told us, my father told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi told me, on the authority of Imran ibn Abi Yahya, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ka’b ibn Malik, on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever takes a bath on Friday and touches some of his family’s perfume if he has any, and puts on his best clothes, then goes out until he comes to the mosque and bows if he wants and does not disturb anyone, then listens when his imam comes out until he prays, it will be an expiation for what happened between that and the next Friday.” And in Sunan Abi Dawud and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam, may God be pleased with him, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say on the pulpit, There is nothing wrong with any of you buying two garments for Friday other than his two garments for work. And on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the pulpit, There is nothing wrong with any of you buying two garments for Friday other than my two garments for work. His profession. Narrated by Ibn Majah. And the Almighty’s saying: When the call is made for the prayer on Friday, what is meant by this call is the second call that was made in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he came out and sat on the pulpit, because at that time the call to prayer was made in front of him, so this is what is meant. As for the first call that was added by the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, this was only due to the large number of people, as narrated by Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, where he said: Adam, he is Ibn Abi Iyas, told us, Ibn Abi Dhi’b, from Al-Zuhri, from Al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid, who said: The call to prayer on Friday began when the imam sat on the pulpit during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr, and Umar. Then, after some time, Uthman came and the number of people increased, he added the second call to prayer from Al-Zawraa, meaning he would call to prayer from the house called Al-Zawraa, which was the highest house in Madinah, near the mosque. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Naim told us, Ibrahim told us, Muhammad ibn Rashid al-Makhuli told us, on the authority of Makhul, that the call to prayer on Fridays used to be given by one muezzin, when the imam came out and then the prayer was established. This was the call at which buying and selling was forbidden when it was called, so Uthman may God be pleased with him ordered that the call be made before the imam came out so that the people could gather. Only free men were ordered to attend Friday prayers, not slaves, women, and children. The traveler, the sick, the caretaker of the sick, and those with similar excuses were excused, as stated in the books of branches. God the Almighty said: And leave off trading meaning, hasten to the remembrance of God and abandon trading when the call to prayer is made. For this reason, scholars may God be pleased with them agreed that trading is forbidden after the second call to prayer. They differed as to whether it is valid if someone engages in it or not. There are two opinions. The apparent meaning of the verse is that it is not valid, as is stated in its place, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: That is better for you, if you only knew meaning, abandoning trading and turning to the remembrance of God and prayer is better for you, that is, in this world and the hereafter, if you only knew. God the Almighty said: So when the prayer is concluded meaning, when it is finished, then disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of God because He restricted their actions after the call to prayer and commanded them to gather, He permitted them after completion to disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of God. This is similar to the way Irak ibn Malik may God be pleased with him used to leave the mosque after the Friday prayer and stand at the door of the mosque and say: O God, I have answered Your call, performed Your obligatory prayer, and dispersed as You commanded me, so provide for me from Your bounty, for You are the best of providers. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. It was narrated from some of the Salaf that he said: Whoever buys and sells on Friday after the prayer, God will bless him seventy times, based on the words of God the Most High: So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of God and His words: And remember God often that you may be successful. That is, when you buy and sell, take and give, remember God often, and do not let this world distract you from that which will benefit you in the Hereafter. For this reason, it was stated in the hadith: “Whoever enters a marketplace and says, ‘There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things,’ God will write for him a million good deeds and erase a million bad deeds from him.” Mujahid said: A servant will not be among those who remember God often until he remembers God standing, sitting and lying down.

The Jews will be tomorrow and the Christians the day after tomorrow.” This is the wording of Al-Bukhari. In a wording of Muslim: “God led those before us astray from Friday, so the Jews had Saturday, and the Christians had Sunday, so God brought us and guided us to Friday, so He made Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. And likewise they will follow us on the Day of Resurrection. We are the last of the people of this world, and the first on the Day of Resurrection, and the judgment will be between them before all creation.” God has commanded the believers to gather to worship Him on Friday, as He says: O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Jumu’ah, then proceed to the remembrance of God. That is, go straight ahead, be intentional, and be attentive in your walk to it. What is meant by striding here is not walking quickly, but rather being attentive to it, as God says: And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the necessary effort while he is a believer. Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with them used to recite it: Then hasten to the remembrance of God. As for walking quickly to prayer, it has been forbidden, as they reported in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “When you hear the call to prayer, then walk to the prayer with tranquility and dignity, and do not rush. Pray whatever you catch up with, and complete whatever you miss.” This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Abu Qatadah said: While we were praying with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he heard the noise of men. When he had finished, he said: What is the matter with you? They said: We rushed to the prayer. He said: "Do not do that. When you come to the prayer, walk and be tranquil. Pray whatever you catch up with, and complete whatever you miss." `Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: "When the prayer is called, do not come running, but come walking, with tranquility and dignity. Pray whatever you catch up with, and complete whatever you miss." At-Tirmidhi narrated it in this way from the hadith of `Abd al-Razzaq. He narrated it via Yazid ibn Zari` from Muammar from al-Zuhri from Abu Salamah from Abu Hurayrah, similarly. Al-Hasan said: By God, it is not about walking on foot, and they were forbidden to come to the prayer except with tranquility and dignity, but with the heart, intention, and humility. Qatada said about His statement: So strive to the remembrance of God meaning that you strive with your heart and your actions, which is walking to it. He interpreted the statement of God Almighty: And when he reached the age of striving with him as meaning walking with him. Something similar was narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Zayd ibn Aslam, and others. It is recommended for the one who comes to the Friday prayer to take a bath before coming to it, as it was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When one of you comes to the Friday prayer, let him take a bath. And they both have on the authority of Abu Sa’id, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Taking a bath on Friday is obligatory for every adult. And on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God’s right over every Muslim is that he take a bath every seven days, washing his head and his body. Narrated by Muslim. And on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is obligatory for every Muslim man every seven days to take a bath on one day, which is Friday. Narrated by Ahmad, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Hibban. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Adam told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of al-Awza’i, on the authority of Hassan ibn Atiyah, on the authority of Abu al-Ash’ath al-San’ani, on the authority of Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafi, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever performs ghusl and bathes on Friday, and comes early and walks and does not ride, and draws close to the imam and listens and does not engage in idle talk, will have for every step the reward of a year of fasting and praying.” This hadith has various chains of transmission and wordings, and it was narrated by the four scholars of Sunan, and al-Tirmidhi classed it as hasan. Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever performs ghusl on Friday, the ghusl for major ritual impurity, then goes in the first hour, it is as if he sacrificed a camel. Whoever goes in the second hour, it is as if he sacrificed a cow. Whoever goes in the third hour, it is as if he sacrificed a horned ram. Whoever goes in the fourth hour, it is as if he sacrificed a chicken. Whoever goes in the fifth hour, it is as if he sacrificed an egg. When the imam comes out, the angels are present and listen to the remembrance.” Narrated by both of them. It is recommended that he wear his best clothes, clean himself, use a miswak, clean himself and purify himself. And in the hadith of Abu Saeed mentioned above, Ghusl on Friday is obligatory for every adult, as is the siwak, and to touch some of his family’s perfume. Imam Ahmad said: Ya’qub told us, my father told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi told me, on the authority of Imran ibn Abi Yahya, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ka’b ibn Malik, on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever takes a bath on Friday and touches some of his family’s perfume if he has any, and puts on his best clothes, then goes out until he comes to the mosque and bows if he wants and does not disturb anyone, then listens when his imam comes out until he prays, it will be an expiation for what happened between that and the next Friday.” And in Sunan Abi Dawud and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam, may God be pleased with him, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say on the pulpit, There is nothing wrong with any of you buying two garments for Friday other than his two garments for work. And on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the pulpit, There is nothing wrong with any of you buying two garments for Friday other than my two garments for work. His profession. Narrated by Ibn Majah. And the Almighty’s saying: When the call is made for the prayer on Friday, what is meant by this call is the second call that was made in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he came out and sat on the pulpit, because at that time the call to prayer was made in front of him, so this is what is meant. As for the first call that was added by the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, this was only due to the large number of people, as narrated by Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, where he said: Adam, he is Ibn Abi Iyas, told us, Ibn Abi Dhi’b, from Al-Zuhri, from Al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid, who said: The call to prayer on Friday began when the imam sat on the pulpit during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr, and Umar. Then, after some time, Uthman came and the number of people increased, he added the second call to prayer from Al-Zawraa, meaning he would call to prayer from the house called Al-Zawraa, which was the highest house in Madinah, near the mosque. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Naim told us, Ibrahim told us, Muhammad ibn Rashid al-Makhuli told us, on the authority of Makhul, that the call to prayer on Fridays used to be given by one muezzin, when the imam came out and then the prayer was established. This was the call at which buying and selling was forbidden when it was called, so Uthman may God be pleased with him ordered that the call be made before the imam came out so that the people could gather. Only free men were ordered to attend Friday prayers, not slaves, women, and children. The traveler, the sick, the caretaker of the sick, and those with similar excuses were excused, as stated in the books of branches. God the Almighty said: And leave off trading meaning, hasten to the remembrance of God and abandon trading when the call to prayer is made. For this reason, scholars may God be pleased with them agreed that trading is forbidden after the second call to prayer. They differed as to whether it is valid if someone engages in it or not. There are two opinions. The apparent meaning of the verse is that it is not valid, as is stated in its place, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: That is better for you, if you only knew meaning, abandoning trading and turning to the remembrance of God and prayer is better for you, that is, in this world and the hereafter, if you only knew. God the Almighty said: So when the prayer is concluded meaning, when it is finished, then disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of God because He restricted their actions after the call to prayer and commanded them to gather, He permitted them after completion to disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of God. This is similar to the way Irak ibn Malik may God be pleased with him used to leave the mosque after the Friday prayer and stand at the door of the mosque and say: O God, I have answered Your call, performed Your obligatory prayer, and dispersed as You commanded me, so provide for me from Your bounty, for You are the best of providers. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. It was narrated from some of the Salaf that he said: Whoever buys and sells on Friday after the prayer, God will bless him seventy times, based on the words of God the Most High: So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of God and His words: And remember God often that you may be successful. That is, when you buy and sell, take and give, remember God often, and do not let this world distract you from that which will benefit you in the Hereafter. For this reason, it was stated in the hadith: “Whoever enters a marketplace and says, ‘There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things,’ God will write for him a million good deeds and erase a million bad deeds from him.” Mujahid said: A servant will not be among those who remember God often until he remembers God standing, sitting and lying down.
62:11: God the Blessed and Most High rebukes what had happened of turning away from the Friday sermon to the trade that had come to Medina on that day, so He the Almighty said: And when they see some trade or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing meaning on the pulpit giving the sermon. This is how it was mentioned by more than one of the Successors, including Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Hasan, Zayd ibn Aslam and Qatadah. Muqatil ibn Hayyan claimed that the trade belonged to Dihya ibn Khalifah before he converted to Islam, and she had a drum with her, so they turned away to it and left the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) standing on the pulpit, except for a few of them. This report has been authenticated, as Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi Al-Ja’d, on the authority of Jabir, who said: A caravan once came to Medina, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was giving the sermon, so the people went out and twelve men remained, so the verse And when they see some trade or amusement, they disperse to it was revealed. They included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Salim with it. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la said: Zakariya bin Yahya told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Salim bin Abi al-Ja`d and Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir bin `Abdullah, who said: While the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was delivering the Friday sermon, a caravan arrived in Madinah and the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) rushed to it until there were only twelve men left with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if you were to continue in succession until not one of you remained, the valley would flow with you in fire. Then this verse was revealed: And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it and leave you standing. He said: Among the twelve who remained steadfast with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were Abu Bakr and `Umar may God be pleased with them. God’s statement: and leave you standing is evidence that the imam delivers the Friday sermon standing. Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had two sermons, between which he would sit and recite the Qur’an and remind the people. However, there is something that should be known, which is that this story was said to have happened when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would perform the Friday prayer before the sermon, as narrated by Abu Dawud in his book, Al-Marasil. Mahmoud ibn Khalid told us on the authority of Al-Walid, Abu Mu’adh ibn Maruf told me that he heard Muqatil ibn Hayyan say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would pray on Friday before the sermon, like the two Eid prayers. Then one day the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was delivering the sermon and had prayed the Friday prayer, a man entered and said: Dihya ibn Khalifah has come with a business transaction. So they dispersed and only a few remained with him. And God, the Most High, said: “Say: ‘What is with God’” meaning what is with God of reward in the Hereafter is better than amusement and trade, and God is the Best of providers meaning for whoever puts his trust in Him and seeks provision in its proper time. End of the interpretation of Surat Al-Jumu’ah. All praise and thanks are due to God, and with Him comes success and protection.
